subject.title: MissingAgentHarnessError race: non-atomic harness registry clear+restore during plugin cache cycle

question: What harness ownership contract should OpenClaw use when plugin reload or empty-scope activation clears the process-global harness registry?
rationale: Current source and the open candidate PR show the remaining blocker is not whether missing harnesses can break turns, but which harnesses may survive an empty or changed plugin scope without weakening plugin disablement semantics.

options.title: Preserve approved always-on harnesses
options.body: Filter preservation to core or maintainer-approved always-on harnesses, clear plugin-owned harnesses outside the active scope, and prove both behaviors in loader and gateway tests.

options.title: Restore every previous harness
options.body: Allow all previously registered harnesses to survive empty-scope reloads, accepting the compatibility and security-boundary implications as intentional product behavior.

options.title: Use retry/readiness only
options.body: Avoid changing registry ownership semantics for now and add bounded retry or readiness gating for channel dispatch, while leaving invalid runtime/plugin states fail-closed.

recommendation.title: Preserve approved always-on harnesses
recommendation.body: Filter preservation to core or maintainer-approved always-on harnesses, clear plugin-owned harnesses outside the active scope, and prove both behaviors in loader and gateway tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The registry contract was introduced in this history and the remaining decision is the core plugin/runtime ownership boundary.
